1  Dated this the 10th day of December, 2024
JUDGMENT
The appeal is preferred by the claimant aggrieved by the award in O.P.(MV)No.1243/2018 on the files of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Vatakara.
2. The claimant/appellant contended that he is a designer and photographer by profession.

He met with an accident on 07.08.2018 at 8.15 P.M, while he was driving a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KL-18-N-3502 to Thalassery and when he reached Chokli, a car bearing Reg.No.KL-18-H-9760 coming from Thalassery side driven in rash and negligent manner came and hit against the petitioner's motorcycle.

Thus the petitioner was thrown down and sustained serious injuries.
3.
In support of the claim, the claimant produced Exts.A1 to A7 documents.
No oral or documentary evidence was adduced on the side of the Insurance Company.
The claimant examined himself as PW1.

As against the claim of monthly 2024:KER:95996 income of Rs.40,000/-, the Tribunal proceeded to fix the notional at Rs.10,500/- and granted the following compensation:

sentences.text: 4. Aggrieved by the insufficiency in the compensation granted as aforesaid, the claimant has approached this Court in the present appeal.

5. Heard, Smt.Seetha M.P. - learned counsel appearing 2024:KER:95996 for the appellant and Sri.Renil Anto Kandamkulathy - learned Standing Counsel for the Insurance Company.
6.

The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that, after concluding that the appellant is a Designer and Photographer by profession and he had to undergo amputation of his right leg, the Tribunal did not grant sufficient compensation towards the disability.
According to the learned counsel, the finding of the Tribunal remains unchallenged.

Still going further, the Tribunal even without any evidence regarding the disabilities, had proceeded to fix the disability in terms of the provisions contained under the Workmens' Compensation Act, 1923, at 60%.
This shows the grievous nature of the injuries suffered by the appellant and therefore, the Tribunal ought to have fixed the monthly income of the deceased at a reasonable amount.

The learned counsel further pointed out that under the non-conventional heads, including the claim for future treatment, the Tribunal has not allowed any compensation for the purchase of prosthesis and also its replacement.
Still further, the compensation granted under the other non-conventional heads are highly inadequate.

On the other hand, Sri.Renil Anto Kandamkulathy - learned Standing Counsel appearing for the Insurance Company, pointed out that except these self-serving statements of the appellant, no evidence was produced before the Tribunal to show that the claimant is a Designer and a Photographer by profession.

It is further pointed out that, though the appellant had undergone amputation for the right leg, the Tribunal had without even referring the claimant to examination by the Medical Board, had fixed the percentage of disability at 60%, which itself is a reasonable assessment made by the Tribunal and thus does not call for any further enhancement by this Court in exercise of its appellate jurisdiction.
8. I have considered the rival submissions raised across the Bar and have perused the impugned award in the appeal.
9. On a close reading of the impugned award, it is explicitly clear that the Tribunal has entered into a categoric finding regarding the avocation of the claimant.

Though the Insurance Company raised serious dispute regarding the avocation, in the absence of any contra evidence, either oral or documentary, this Court has to necessarily go by the version of 2024:KER:95996 PW1, the claimant,
and also the findings rendered by the Tribunal in this regard.
Thus, it has to be concluded that the claimant's profession as a Designer and a Photographer stood unequivocally proved before the Tribunal.
10. The claimant/appellant having been successful in proving the avocation, the next question before this Court would be what should be the notional income of the claimant.
It is pertinent to mention that the accident took place on 07.08.2018.

sentences.text: Considering the qualification and avocation of the claimant in the peculiar facts and circumstances of this case, this Court is of the considered view that an amount of Rs.25,000/- can be fixed as the notional income of the claimant.
The percentage of disability being more than 50%, the claimant is also entitled for grant of future prospects.
Therefore, he is entitled to get 40% as future prospects.

11. Coming forward to the claim of prosthesis, it has to be noticed by this Court that the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Vivek 2024:KER:95996 G. v. National Insurance Company Ltd. [2023 KHC 2941], which was followed by this Court in Deepa Cyrus v. the Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. [MACA No.1577/2021] decided on 30.10.2024, that the claim for prosthesis has to be granted even if it is not sought for.

entities.text: Vivek 2024:KER:95996 G. v. National Insurance Company Ltd. [2023 KHC 2941]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Deepa Cyrus v. the Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. [MACA No.1577/2021]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Going by the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Vivek (supra), this Court is of the considered view that the appellant is entitled for a claim for prosthesis.
It is now settled that the prosthesis has to be changed for every five years, or has to be repaired suitably by expending considerable amount within a period of two to three years.
Considering the age of the claimant and also his avocation, this Court is of the considered view that the claimant could be granted compensation for change of prosthesis for three times.
The question however would be, what should be the amount fixed for change of prosthesis.
It must be noticed that no evidence has been adduced before the Tribunal to prove exactly what would be the cost of prosthesis.
In such circumstance, this Court is left with no other options, but to undertake a reasonable assessment regarding the claim for prosthesis.
Therefore, this Court is of the 2024:KER:95996 considered view that an amount of Rs.2.5 lakhs can be granted for one prosthesis and thus a total of Rs.7.5 lakhs towards three prosthesis replacement.
12. In respect of other conventional heads like marriage prospects and attendance at home, this Court is of the considered view that a reasonable compensation could be granted by this Court.
13. In the result of the above discussions, the appellant is entitled to succeed.
The appeal stands allowed.

The enhanced compensation to which the appellant is entitled to is as follows:
The notional income of the deceased is fixed at Rs.25,000/-.
Adding 40% future prospects to the notional income comes to Rs.35,000/-.

 Accordingly, the appellant/claimant is awarded an additional compensation of Rs.34,07,060/- (Rupees thirty four lakhs seven thousand sixty only) over and above the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
While calculating interest, the claimant/appellant will not be entitled to interest on the claim for prosthesis.
The interest shall be calculated only on the amount Rs.26,57,060/- @ 8% per annum from the date of petition till realization together with proportionate costs.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the aforesaid amount within a period of 30 days two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
The appeal is allowed accordingly.
